== /workspace/runbook/decimal-fix.md
# Decimal-aggregation fix (meter 2026.41)

The aggregator in the running build (2026.38) truncates at the fourth decimal when it sums metered units
across shards instead of rounding. Large accounts come out a few thousandths under; the October finance
recon caught it.

2026.41 carries the correction. QA signed it off on 2026-10-30 and it is staged as the executable
usage-db-5 will run at its next start (see /workspace/usage-db-5/startup.json).

After the engine comes up, the post-start checks re-aggregate a sample day against the corrected
reference and confirm the billable totals are exact. Watch them with the restart status tool.
== /workspace/runbook/lease-broker.md
# Destination-lease broker (lease-broker-02)

Owner: identity platform. On call: whoever holds the platform pager (this week: you).

The metering service never talks to usage-db-5 directly. Every client — the six meter pollers, the
rollup reader, the billing-export job — holds a signed lease that names its destination. Leases are
signed at issuance and cannot be called back early; a client drops the route the moment its lease runs
out. While a destination stays eligible, the broker keeps issuing and renewing leases for it, so a live
destination always has a couple of dozen outstanding.

Each lease carries one pooled session into the engine. A session closes once its lease has run out and
its open statements have finished (statements time out after 5s).

Pieces you operate:

- leasecat — the ledger: which destinations are eligible, and the outstanding leases per destination.
- leasebridge — a per-destination hold in front of the engine: arriving statements wait in a bridge
  queue while the statements already inside the engine finish or hit their timeout.
- ledgerdb — the engine itself: a restart brings it up on whatever executable is staged for the next
  start, then runs the post-start checks.

Engine notes: usage-db-5 keeps its data on durable volume pgdata-5, reattached at every start. An engine
stop aborts whatever statements are in flight at that moment; aborted usage writes are lost for good and
the day's rollup is flagged suspect from then on.
